story.title: Pope Leo XIV's First Images Released Post-Surgery
story.summary: The Vatican has shared the first images of Pope Leo XIV following his surgery to remove a cancerous tumor from his right lung. Doctors report that the 71-year-old pontiff is showing steady improvement after the procedure, which took place on Tuesday.

timeline_highlights.title: Pope Leo XIV Discharged from Hospital After Lung Cancer Surgery
timeline_highlights.summary: Pope Leo XIV was discharged from Gemelli Hospital in Rome on Saturday after undergoing surgery to remove a cancerous tumor from his right lung. The 71-year-old pontiff had part of his lung removed and was deemed fit for discharge by his doctors, who confirmed his diagnosis of lung cancer earlier this week.

He was discharged from the hospital four days after the operation.
Doctors confirmed he has lung cancer.

event_overview.title: About Health and Recovery
event_overview.subject: Health and Recovery
event_overview.summary: This event concerns Pope Leo XIV’s hospitalization and recovery after thoracic surgery at Rome’s Agostino Gemelli University Hospital. During the October 13, 2026 procedure, doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung; an intraoperative examination confirmed lung adenocarcinoma, and the Holy See said the operation had no complications.

facts.label: Surgery date
facts.value: Pope Leo XIV underwent the scheduled operation on October 13, 2026.

facts.label: Location
facts.value: The procedure and postoperative care took place at the Agostino Gemelli University Hospital in Rome, Italy.

facts.label: Procedure and diagnosis
facts.value: Doctors used a video-assisted technique to remove the lower lobe of the Pope’s right lung; intraoperative histology confirmed lung adenocarcinoma that had been suspected in preoperative testing.

facts.label: Medical team
facts.value: The thoracic surgery team was led by Professor Stefano Margaritora; the postoperative updates were issued by Dr. Luigi Carbone and Professor Margaritora through the Holy See Press Office.

facts.label: Initial recovery status
facts.value: As of October 16, 2026, the Holy See reported that blood tests and a chest X-ray showed steady improvement, while the Pope continued respiratory physiotherapy and independently performed normal daily activities.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the immediate October 14–16, 2026 recovery updates and public reappearance following surgery, not the Pope’s complete medical history, pathology workup, or any later treatment decisions.

related_stories.title: Children Bear Heavy Toll in DRC's Severe Ebola Outbreak
related_stories.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo is experiencing its deadliest Ebola outbreak, with children particularly affected. Reports indicate that more than 1 in 4 of the deaths are among children, who face a staggering 60% fatality rate. This outbreak is caused by a rare strain of the virus for which there is currently no approved treatment.

related_stories.title: Three Men Sentenced to 158 Years for Murdering Surfers in Mexico
related_stories.summary: A Mexican judge has sentenced three men to 158 years and nine months in prison each for the murders of Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their American friend Carter Rhoad. The trio was killed during a surfing trip in Baja California in 2024, reportedly during an attempted robbery.
